reading.body:
Melva Wallace is president and CEO of Huston-Tillotson University in Austin, Texas, and the AI ecosystem dataset files her under Advocates and Public Voices.

That category assignment is the only thing connecting her to AI. The record lists one field, higher education administration, one timeline entry marked Current, and no initiative, program, publication, or statement about artificial intelligence. The hook and the achievement both say the same thing, that she leads a historically Black university in Austin.

If the link is real, it would run through institutions rather than infrastructure. Universities supply the people who build and operate AI systems, and a sitting president is a plausible voice in that pipeline. But nothing in the data establishes that role, and the record carries no compute, building, or power information at all, so it cannot speak to the constraints that govern AI scaling.

What the data does not cover is most of what a reader would want. There are no dates beyond a single Current marker, no tenure, no enrollment or budget figures, no AI-related activity, and no relationship to any other entity in the dataset. The sourcing is one LinkedIn profile with no secondary confirmation, so the title itself is the whole of the evidence.
